name: Winsorize the wild claim at the day fence
non_visual_rationale: A fence is a bound between two stored numbers; no surface exists. No template, string, style or route is touched, and at launch the observation log is empty so the published surface is byte-identical. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
criteria_delivered: 1. With three or more device-samples on a day, residuals are clipped to two band widths either side of the spot-day median. Two BAND WIDTHS OF THE DAY MEDIAN'S OWN BAND, pinned as the roadmap asked: a fence measured in the clipped sample's band would let a wilder claim buy itself a wider fence.

2. A wild claim moves the stored difference EXACTLY as far as a claim pinned at the fence moves it, and no further -- proven as equality against a twin run rather than as a corridor -- and still moves it, proven against a third run where the same reporter saw what everyone else saw. Down-weight, never ban: the claim is pulled back to the fence, never dropped.

3. Below three device-samples no same-day robustification applies. Proven by the same twin trick: a wild claim on a two-witness morning stores exactly what the same claim stores on a morning nobody else reported, which is only true if no fence touched either.

4. THE 04-01 CRITERION CARRIED FORWARD: the collapse runs before the fence, in the 06 section 6.2 order. A wild claim submitted three times stores the bytes it stores submitted once; fencing first would let the three repeats become the morning's median and fence the two honest reporters instead.
scope_note: The accepted roadmap names weights.ts and the unit laws. residuals.ts was also touched, and had to be: the fence is measured in band widths, and the band token is consumed and dropped where the residual is formed, so the sample has to carry its width forward. correction-file.ts was touched for the same reason 04-01 touched it -- the weighing room has to reach the one place a key's evidence is counted. The roadmap's 'FIRST MOVE: delete its entry from PENDING_SLICES' line is stale boilerplate naming a cucumber scaffold this feature does not have; see 04-01's scope_note for the full record.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: AN OPEN-ENDED MEDIAN MEANS NO FENCE, NOT AN INVENTED WIDTH. The roadmap's PIN says the fence is two widths of the day median's band, '(finite by construction; the open band has no width)'. It does not say what happens when the day's median report IS the open top band. 06 section 5.1 gives that band a nominal 3.0 m value and a nominal 0.25 variance standing in for its missing upper edge -- neither of those is a width, and deriving one from the variance (sqrt(12 * 0.25) = 1.73 m) would be a manufactured number dressed as a measurement. So a morning whose middle report is open-ended has no fence and stands exactly as it was reported, the same answer the rule already gives below three device-samples. This is the project's one rule applied literally: if a number cannot be computed honestly, do not invent one. The unit property covers the branch directly.

A SCORE RESIDUAL IS NEVER FENCED, for the same reason: it is a difference between two points on the 0-100 ladder and was never reported as an interval, so it has no width and no fence can be measured in it. This falls out of the width being null rather than needing a branch at the call site.

'THREE OR MORE DEVICE-SAMPLES' IS COUNTED AS 'THREE OR MORE SAMPLES', which is exact only because the fence runs after 04-01's collapse, where a day already holds at most one sample per device. Recorded because it is a coupling between two steps rather than a property of this one: reversing the order would silently change what the threshold counts, which is what criterion 4's test now forbids.

THE FENCE CLIPS THE VALUE AND NOTHING ELSE. The sample keeps its own precision weight, its own reporter and its own day. The precision weight is a property of the band the person reported, not of the number the fit was willing to believe, and re-deriving it from the clipped value would credit a fenced claim with a certainty its reporter never expressed.
acceptance: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/a-wild-claim-is-pulled-to-the-day-fence.test.ts, three examples over the real runLearningFitOnce port. Twenty-two mornings at one spot, all chest-to-head (1.1 m to 1.6 m, so the fence is 2 x 0.5 = 1.0 m), plus one reporter whose claim is the knob and, in the three-deep runs, one extra honest witness on that morning. THE ORACLE IS A TWIN RUN throughout: the fenced claim and a claim pinned exactly at the fence carry the same band, so the same precision weight, and after clipping the same value, so the two runs must store the same number to the last digit. The pinned twin gets an hour of its own on that morning with a forecast row sized for it, which is the only way to place a residual exactly on the fence when the reported bands are a discrete table. THE WILD CLAIM IS ANKLE-TO-KNEE, not the open top band the roadmap sketched, and the reason is recorded in the test header: an open-ended claim has no width, so on a two-report morning it is the median that carries no fence at all and the run comes out identical whether the fence fires at two device-samples or at three. That fixture could not prove criterion 3, and the mutation pass caught it -- see the N2 record below. Ankle-to-knee is also the hazard research 09 section 13.5c actually names: under-reporting a spot to keep it empty.
unit_law: Three fast-check properties in tests/unit/learning-weight-laws.test.ts against winsorizeAtDayFence, whose exported signature is its port. (1) INVARIANT over generated three-to-nine-report mornings: no residual leaves the fence the day median's own band allows, the fence only ever pulls a claim TOWARD the middle, no report is dropped, and no claim changes its weight, its person or its morning. The property also carries the open-ended branch: when the middle report named no width, every value must come back untouched. (2) INVARIANT over one- and two-report mornings: the list comes back deep-equal to the way it was reported. (3) IDEMPOTENCE over a free mixture of mornings, which is what forbids a fence that walks inward on every pass.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) a well-watched wild claim is pulled to the fence and no further, while still being heard, (2) below three device-samples nothing is robustified, (3) the collapse runs before the fence. Three behaviours, budget 6. Delivered 6: 3 acceptance examples and 3 unit properties.
red_evidence: The acceptance test was written first and run against the 04-01 body. RED with a semantic AssertionError: 'a double-overhead claim moved the stored difference to -0.22949069799683197, past the -0.21503977723568124 a claim pinned at the day's fence reaches: the claim was believed instead of fenced'. Its two companion examples passed on arrival, correctly -- with no fence in the code the two-witness run and the alone run already agree, and the collapse ordering example is vacuously true until a second stage exists to be ordered against. Both became load-bearing at GREEN, which mutations N2 and N3 confirm. The three unit properties were run against the absent function first and failed at collection, so they were re-run against the real body and each was then falsified by its own targeted mutation below rather than resting on that.
falsifiability_evidence: Five controlled mutations, each planted alone against a byte-snapshot of src/learning, each reverted, the revert verified with diff -r ('REVERT CLEAN: src/learning matches the pre-mutation snapshot byte for byte'), the suite re-run green. (N1) the fence measured in the CLIPPED sample's own band instead of the day median's -- the mutation that would let a wilder claim buy a wider fence: caught twice, by the unit invariant ('a residual of 0.6000000000010001 sits outside the 0 +/- 0.6 the day's fence allows') and by the acceptance twin. (N2) the fence firing at two device-samples instead of three: caught by the below-three property AND by the acceptance twin ('two device-samples on one morning stored -0.15495913121160004 where the same claim standing alone stored -0.1503787883391775'). THIS ONE IS THE FINDING OF THE STEP: on the first fixture, where the wild claim named the open top band, N2 was invisible to acceptance and only the unit property caught it, because an open-ended median carries no fence and the mutation therefore changed nothing. The fixture was moved to a band with two edges and re-run; the acceptance example now catches it too. (N3) the morning fenced BEFORE the session was collapsed: caught by the ordering example, which is exactly what that example exists for. (N4) a claim past the fence dropped instead of pulled back to it -- censoring instead of winsorizing: caught by 'fencing a morning must never drop a report' and by the twin runs no longer weighing the same mornings. (N5) an open-ended median given an invented 0.5 m width instead of no fence: caught by the open-ended branch of the invariant.
